walkthroughs.body_html: SSRIs: work in 2-6 weeks but cause side effects (nausea, insomnia). CBT: takes longer but lowers relapse rates because clients learn skills. NICE recommends both, often combined, for moderate-severe depression.
CBT strength: tackles the cause, long-lasting; weakness: requires effort and good rapport. Drug strength: fast, easy to take; weakness: treats symptoms, not causes, plus dependence risk.

For a teen with mild depression, NICE recommends starting with talking therapy like CBT before drugs. For severe cases, SSRIs may be combined with CBT. Always consider side effects, age and patient preference.
